issues.title: Commits delivery using GSA_REKEY
issues.author: smyslov
issues.body: For scalability reasons, it would be desirable to re-use GSA_REKEY pseudo-exchange to fan out MLS commits.

issues.title: Make only group senders responsible for creating MLS commits
issues.author: smyslov
issues.body:
Currently any GM can be used by the GCKS to ask for MLS commits. I think that this should be limited to group senders only.
Requesting commits requites a unicast IKE SA between the GCKS and a GM. RFC 9838 already proposes that in large groups with small number of senders (e.g. live broadcast) the GCKS can maintain unicast IKE SA to senders and use multicast GSA_REKEY to deliver updates to receivers. This ensures that no interruption of traffic happens if network is lossy - update to senders is reliable.

comments.author: smyslov
comments.body: Jus a thought - shouldn't those GMs that are not senders, act as partial MLS clients (as per draft-ietf-mls-partial)? I'm thinking on scenarios like live broadcasting, when there is a single sender and a lot of (sometimes constrained) receivers.

issues.title: Re-use existing G-IKEv2 registries for MLS objects
issues.author: smyslov
issues.body: Currently the draft uses the only new G-IKEv2 attribute mls_commit` object for wrapping all MLS objects. THe type of MLS object is determined by additional value MlsGikeObjectType inside this attribute. This would require creating a new IANA registry to manage these types. Instead, we can use the existing IANA registries for G-IKEv2 attributes and allocate a separate attribute for each MLS object.

pulls.title: Multicast GSA_REKEY with optional LKH protection
pulls.author: kkohbrok

comments.author: smyslov
comments.body: Again, perhaps the best is to merge the PR "as is" and then do some refining pass if needed.

For multicast fan out using GSA_REKEY, AUTH_KEY is needed. It contains a GCKS's public key, that is provided to a GM at the time of registration, so that when multicast rekey message is received, the GM can verify its signature.
In addition, WRAP_KEY attributes are needed for LKH. They contain the path (a sequence of keys when each next is encrypted, or wrapped, with the previous) in the logical key tree for a GM. This path in a tree is specific for each GM (as they are leafs in the tree), so later the GCKS can craft a message that, while being received by all GMs, would not be possible to decrypt for the excluded GM.

The GCKS first rekeys the REkey SA itseld using LKH, thus leaving the excluded GM an ability to decrypt multicast messages on new Rekey SA. Then it can fan-out MLS objects installing new Data-security SA using a new Rekey SA. The excluded GM will be able to see this message, but unable to decrypt it. Just for clarification.
I think this is true even if GSA_REKEY is not used :-)
AUTH_KEY and WRAP_KEY are Member Key Bag attributes. And they are needed for multicast GSA_REKEY (WRAP_KEY - in case of LKH).
This should be 2-staged: first rekey the Rekey SA (and exclude a GM) and then distribute the MLS objects. Thus, 2 messages must be depicted.

True, but needs clarification. The Rekey SA keys are always generated and provided exclusively by the GCKS (as well as all wrap keys for LKH). This is from G-IKEv2 and is not changed. The second part is obvious and does not depend on whether multicast rekey or inband rekey is used.

pulls.title: Consistensy + few design proposals
pulls.author: smyslov
pulls.body:
Mostly editorial changes to keep text consistent, but also few design proposals:
1. Return MLS object to the candidate GM in the GSA_AUTH response on registration. Unless I'm missing something with MLS message sequencing, I think this is more streamlined, the GCKS just delays this response until it contacts the designated GM and receives the commit message.
2. Remove any explicit policy for selecting the designated GM/ Afterall, this is a GCKS' local matter. In particular, one of the condition is that there is a persistent unicast IKE SA from this GM to GCKS
3. Add a limitation that only GMs acting as senders can request Path Refresh. I believe that this is reasonable for two reasons - usually senders are in a better position with regard to how often the key should be changed, sinse they know for sure how much traffic is protected using one key. In addition, there must be a persistent unicast IKE SA to the GCKS, and senders will have it often, as their rekeying must be reliable.
4. Rename new exchanges to always start with GSA_ and to have a relatively short name.

comments.body: Sounds good to me. I think you can then remove [these lines](https://github.com/kkohbrok/draft-kohbrok-ipsecme-mls-gike/pull/9/changes#diff-20c57a601bb1c75d7985184dc7f07bd423afd635f539591ea273eb7fbf6063f5R643-R645) from the Security Considerations.
Is this restriction really necessary? If we don't allow non-group sender to issue commits, those members can't update their MLS key material and thus don't gain post-compromise security.

The intent here is to make sure that other GMs don't accept traffic from the removed GM anymore. Any idea for a good wording?

Maybe something like

> If that delivery is not possible, the GCKS needs another authenticated
  mechanism, such as an IKE Delete or Notify, to ensure that the removed GM is
  no longer authorized to participate in the group.  In particular, remaining
  GMs need to stop accepting Data-Security SA traffic from the removed GM,
  either by deleting the old SA, by applying receiver-side Sender-ID filtering,
  or by another policy that prevents use of the removed GM's previous sending
  authorization.

Do you mean the text from Open Questions?

   The designated committer policy needs review.  The policy specified
   before uses the lowest non-blank eligible leaf because it is
   deterministic and easy to specify

Or am some other text? I failed to find related text in the Security Considerations...

Sorry, the link doesn't seem to work. I meant these lines:

> A designated committer can deny service by refusing to commit a GCKS-authored Proposal.
The mitigation specified here is for the GCKS to retry with another non-blank leaf.
More advanced committer selection and reputation policies are not specified in this document.

It is not absolutely necessary, but I have some arguments for this. 

Senders are usually more credible GMs and they are in a better position to count the traffic, so that they know when it's time to change the traffic key to not exceed maximum allowed amount of encrypted data per a key. In addition, if there are few senders (consider live broadcast scenario), then for GCKS it is preferrable to keep unicast IKE SA to them, which is required to request key update.

On the other hand, receiving-only GMs can go up and down (I'm again thinking about live broadcast) and cannot count the amount of traffic reliablly. In addition, for the same live broadcast use case there may be millions of passive GMs and the only way to deliver MLS objects to them is to use multicast Rekey SA. In this case the GCKS most likely will not keep millions unicast IKE SAs to these GMs, which makes impossible for them to request key update. 

I'm very much in doubt that in case the key is really compromise this event will be noticed by a host and any will be action taken upon, like key update, so in my opinion the only realistic scenario is to change the key proactively in a timly fashion, and for this senders are better suited.
I think this text can retain, no need to delete it. Perhaps only the last sentence...

Perhaps I do not see a problem here. If MLS allows to remove GM from the group, the a new SA is created, which automatically deletes the current SA (after DTD). And the removed GM does not have keys for this new SA. Then it should be removed from GCKS' Rekey SA and LKH can be used for this. 

Perhaps the lack of explicit notification to the GM that it is removed is unplesant, but that is that - it's multicast.
